concerns.concern: The Kondo temperature estimate used to rule out Kondo physics plugs in the 80 meV width of the 1T narrow band instead of the unmeasured 1T–1H hybridization width Γ. Because the result is exponentially sensitive to Γ, this only excludes Γ ≈ W₀, not Kondo screening.
concerns.quote: It uses the Haldane-type formula with W₀, the 80 meV width of the 1T narrow band, in place of the hybridization width Γ.

concerns.concern: The width-versus-temperature analysis ignores tip thermal broadening and compares only with a Kondo curve fixed at T_K = 40 K. A free-T_K Kondo fit (~7 K) may reproduce the data, and a linear-in-T width with a finite intercept does not discriminate the two pictures.
concerns.quote: A linear-in-T width over 0.3–4.2 K does not by itself discriminate the two pictures.

concerns.concern: The temperature window crosses T_c = 3 K. Below T_c the 1H bath is gapped, which modifies any Kondo resonance, so the series should be repeated above H_c2.
concerns.quote: The 0.3–4.2 K window straddles T_c = 3 K. Below T_c the 1H bath is gapped (Δ ≈ 0.5 meV, comparable to the peak width)

concerns.concern: The supporting evidence offered against Kondo physics is equally consistent with a Kondo resonance: the Fano line shapes used in the fits and the g ≈ 2 Zeeman splitting.
concerns.quote: Zeeman splitting with g ≈ 2 (Supplementary Fig. 10) is the textbook field response of a Kondo resonance.

concerns.concern: The onset field of the Zeeman splitting should be reported relative to the zero-field width, since Kondo physics predicts splitting only above a field set by T_K.
concerns.quote: The onset field of the splitting relative to the zero-field width. Kondo predicts splitting only for gμ_B B ≳ 0.5 k_B T_K.

concerns.concern: The dependence of the peak width on filling should be used to test Brinkman–Rice scaling (width ∝ doping) against the exponential Kondo form. This requires extending the data to clusters near zero central-peak weight.
concerns.quote: BR predicts Z ∝ doping (δ = 1 − n), i.e. width → 0 linearly as n → 1

concerns.concern: An independent estimate of the 1T–1H hybridization is needed, either from DFT of the actual 4Hb bilayer or from experimental Fano/tunnelling parameters.
concerns.quote: An independent estimate of the 1T–1H hybridization, from DFT of the actual 4Hb bilayer or from the experimental tunnelling-asymmetry/Fano parameters.

concerns.concern: Isolated high-filling clusters embedded in a ~0.2-filled host form an Anderson-impurity problem, not a uniformly doped Hubbard lattice. Lattice Brinkman–Rice/DMFT comparisons at uniform filling therefore do not model the system, and the 'Kondo versus coherent band' framing is partly ill-posed.
concerns.quote: That is an Anderson-impurity problem, so the paper's own framing of "Kondo versus coherent band" is partly ill-posed.

concerns.concern: The authors should show how a cluster's spectrum depends on its neighbours' fillings (isolated versus paired or tripled clusters) and state the length scale over which filling is defined.
concerns.quote: Show how a cluster's spectrum depends on the fillings of its neighbours.

concerns.concern: The authors should either justify why a local spectrum should mimic lattice DMFT or perform an inhomogeneous calculation. This would be a single correlated site of variable filling in a 0.2-filled host plus a 1H bath.
concerns.quote: Either justify why the local spectrum should mimic the lattice DMFT one, or perform an inhomogeneous calculation

concerns.concern: The 0.2 e starting filling comes from integrating dI/dV, which is sensitive to background subtraction, matrix elements and setpoint. Its spin counting is also ambiguous.
concerns.quote: This is sensitive to background subtraction, matrix-element energy dependence, and the setpoint condition

concerns.concern: No explicit, error-barred conversion is given from the hump shift or ε to electron filling n, yet figures use ε as a filling axis and the text claims an approach to half filling.
concerns.quote: the paper never presents the mapping from the −0.5 eV hump shift (only ~80 meV in total, Fig. 2e x-axis) or from ε to n.

concerns.concern: Normalization by high-energy weight shows a ~30% spread, which matters for the small central-peak weights. The robustness of the extracted weights to the setpoint should be shown.
concerns.quote: Fig. 2e shows a ~30% spread (≈200–280 a.u.), which matters at the 1–15% level of the central-peak weight in Fig. 3e.

concerns.concern: The authors should state whether any cluster actually reaches half filling, which would appear as a gapped spectrum without a central peak.
concerns.quote: State whether any cluster actually reaches n = 1, which would appear as a gapped spectrum without a central peak.

concerns.concern: The Se origin of the doping rests only on matching the zero-bias-peak cluster fraction to Se statistics. This ignores the full distribution of intermediate states and complications from Se in 1H layers and the invisible bottom S plane.
concerns.quote: If one Se per cluster produces doping, the full distribution, not only the ZBP fraction, must be accounted for.

concerns.concern: No mechanism is given for why isovalent Se would locally suppress charge transfer, beyond citing a reference.
concerns.quote: No mechanism is given for why isovalent Se suppresses charge transfer locally, beyond citing Ref. 38.

concerns.concern: The most direct test is missing: correlating top-layer Se sites identified in topography with cluster spectra in the same field of view.
concerns.quote: The most direct test is missing: correlating top-layer Se sites (identifiable in bias-dependent topography) with cluster spectra in the same FOV.

concerns.concern: The higher-Se and strain controls are not quantified. Missing are EDX Se content, ZBP fraction, the full hump-energy histogram, strain magnitude and evidence for a reduced c-axis spacing.
concerns.quote: Supplementary Note 4 should quantify the higher-Se sample (Se content measured by EDX, ZBP fraction, full histogram of hump energy) and the applied strain

concerns.concern: Alternative origins of the local filling variation are not addressed, such as CDW phase slips, domain boundaries or an intrinsic first-order transition.
concerns.quote: Alternatives should be addressed, e.g. local CDW phase slips or domain boundaries, or the intrinsic first-order transition of Ref. 28.

concerns.concern: The quoted U, W and U/W values are inconsistent (190/80 ≈ 2.4 versus the stated ~2 and the 1.67 used in DMFT), and W₀ is not the full or unrenormalized bandwidth. The claim of sitting at the border of the Mott criterion is not quantified against U_c1/U_c2.
concerns.quote: U ≈ 190 meV and W₀ ≈ 80 meV give U/W₀ ≈ 2.4, yet the text states ~2 and the DMFT uses U/W = 1.67

concerns.concern: The DFT is for monolayer 1T-TaS₂ with unstated details (spin–orbit coupling, relaxation, band isolation) and omits the 4Hb heterostructure and 1T–1H hybridization. A 4Hb calculation could cross-check the 0.2 e filling.
concerns.quote: The DFT is for a monolayer 1T-TaS₂. The paper does not state spin–orbit coupling, structural relaxation, or how the narrow band was isolated

concerns.concern: The DMFT spectra are compared with experiment only qualitatively. Quantitative comparisons are needed for Z(n), width versus n, the LHB/UHB weight ratio and Hubbard-band positions in meV.
concerns.quote: The DMFT spectra (Fig. 3g, plotted versus E/U) are not compared quantitatively with experiment.

concerns.concern: The fitting procedure is unclear: why Lorentzians in one figure and Fano fits in another, and what the q values are. The fits also miss visible structure; free parameters, background, error bars, decomposition uniqueness and the U–ε covariance are not given.
concerns.quote: Three Lorentzians are used in Fig. 3b, but Fano fits in Fig. 3f; the reason for the switch, and the q values, should be given.

concerns.concern: The central-peak widths should be compared with the lock-in modulation used for each dataset. With a 2 mV modulation for some data, the claim of 'unsurpassed energy resolution' is inappropriate.
concerns.quote: V_mod = 2 meV for Fig. 2 makes "unsurpassed energy resolution" inappropriate for those data.

concerns.concern: The 1T superconducting gap lacks quantitative characterization: Δ_1T versus filling with fit error bars, and the full temperature dependence versus Δ_1H. Data at 3.0 K (equal to T_c) do not show closure above T_c.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4b shows only 0.3 K and 3.0 K; 3.0 K equals T_c, so it does not demonstrate closure "above T_c".

concerns.concern: On zero-bias-peak clusters, a sharp peak could mask a small gap, so field- and temperature-dependent spectra are needed to establish that the gap is truly zero.
concerns.quote: On ZBP clusters, a sharp zero-bias peak can mask a small gap. Show field- and temperature-dependent spectra there to establish Δ = 0.

concerns.concern: Suppression of superconductivity on correlated clusters could come from local-moment pair breaking or a different DOS at E_F, rather than Brinkman–Rice renormalization. These alternatives are not distinguished.
concerns.quote: The suppression could arise from pair breaking by the local moment, or from the different DOS at E_F, rather than from BR renormalization

concerns.concern: If 12% of clusters carry local moments, Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states would be expected in the adjacent 1H layer but none are seen. This constraint on exchange coupling should be discussed.
concerns.quote: If 12% of clusters carry local moments, YSR states would be expected in the adjacent 1H layer, yet none are seen on the 1H termination.

concerns.concern: The same central peak is described both as a coherent Brinkman–Rice quasiparticle band and as localized moments with rigid g = 2 splitting, which is contradictory. The splitting data should move to the main text with field range, onset, filling dependence and spectra above and below H_c2.
concerns.quote: The same central peak is described as a BR coherent band with vanishing width and also as localized moments with g ≈ 2 Zeeman splitting.

concerns.concern: The surface 1T layer has a 1H neighbour on only one side, so its charge transfer may differ from the bulk. Bulk conclusions (π-shifts, magnetic memory) drawn from surface data should be discussed and toned down.
concerns.quote: Bulk-level conclusions (π-shifts in Little–Parks [30], magnetic memory [33]) are drawn from surface data. Please discuss this, and tone down the bulk implications

concerns.concern: Only ~100 or ~30 'typical' spectra are shown out of ~4000 clusters. Selection criteria, full histograms, numbers of samples, cleaves and tips, tip consistency and per-figure measurement temperatures are needed.
concerns.quote: Fig. 2a contains ~4000 clusters, but Fig. 2d uses ~100 "typical" spectra, and Fig. 4e ~30.

concerns.concern: A complementary uniformly tuned filling series (alkali deposition, gating, or varying Se across crystals) is suggested to test the lattice Brinkman–Rice picture directly.
concerns.quote: If feasible, a complementary uniformly tuned filling series would directly test whether the lattice BR picture holds.

concerns.concern: The nominal Se content in the Methods (1% of S) conflicts with the 0.5% substitution quoted in the text, and these should be reconciled with the EDX result.
concerns.quote: The Methods give a nominal Se of 1% of S, while the text quotes 0.5% substitution; reconcile these with the EDX result.

concerns.concern: There are figure-reference and caption errors: a wrong panel citation, a supplementary figure cited for two different contents, and a mismatch between the ε of Fig. 3h and the 'near half filling' claim in the text.
concerns.quote: p. 5: "vanishes (its spectral weight, Fig. 3g)" should be Fig. 3e.

concerns.concern: There are unit and parameter typos: meV versus mV, a modulation value missing units, and inconsistent cluster counts between caption and text.
concerns.quote: "V_s = −10 meV" etc. should be mV.

concerns.concern: There are wording errors and typos, and overstated terms such as 'unprecedented/unsurpassed'.
concerns.quote: "first principal", "exhibit large a Mott gap", "This saturation is unique" (situation?)

concerns.concern: Reference details need correcting: Ref. 44's citation and Ref. 38's article number.
concerns.quote: Ref. 44 should read Rev. Mod. Phys. 68, 13 (1996). Please check Ref. 38's article number.
